record.name: Bhutan
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The 2025 National AI Strategy proposes a national AI governing body and ethical guidelines but no model-evaluation body.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. The retained national-language queries do not adequately target an AI safety or evaluation institute. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

Re-ran searches in English and Dzongkha for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified. Kept low: the Dzongkha query could not be validated by the searcher, so national-language coverage is still not established. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

searches.query: Bhutan artificial intelligence safety institute government
Bhutan national AI policy site.gov.bt responsible
Bhutan AI safety institute national AI governing body GovTech evaluation 2026

check.language_note: The recorded dz query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Some submitted strings contain site. rather than site:; these literal strings are preserved and are not treated as domain-restricted searches. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. Preserved result batches, using 1-based positions in check.searches: BT-dz-search = searches 1, 2 (dz, dz); BT-search = searches 3, 4 (en, en). Each multi-query batch has only a combined returned result set; its source_ids cannot be attributed to individual queries. Historical query dates are recorded as 17 October 2026 in the phase6 search-boundary ledger. The retained Dzongkha query terms were not validated as an adequate search for an AI safety or evaluation institute; this limits confidence to low. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English and Dzongkha; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: The retrieved GovTech strategy and civil-service AI guideline provide substantive primary governance evidence. Formal strategy approval remains unconfirmed. Confidence stays low because the retained Dzongkha queries do not establish an adequate national-language check for an AI safety or evaluation institute.

related_bodies.name: GovTech Agency
related_bodies.role: It drafted the National AI Strategy 2025 and leads digital policy.

related_bodies.name: National AI governing body (proposed)
related_bodies.role: The strategy lists the proposed governing body as an action under its governance enabler. No mandate to evaluate models was stated.

record.notes:
The strategy describes gaps in AI oversight, accountability, transparency and risk safeguards. Its governance actions include a national AI governing body and framework; formal approval by the GovTech Commission was not confirmed, and the proposed body has no stated remit to evaluate advanced models.

The cover of the official civil-service generative-AI usage guideline is dated 2024; the document concerns responsible adoption by the civil service. Searches covered indexed public English and Dzongkha sources for a government-designated AI safety institute with a remit to evaluate advanced models.

next_check.reason: Whether the strategy is formally approved and the national AI governing body is given a mandate.
